en.name: Nicholas of Flue
en.summary: Swiss farmer, soldier, and father of ten who left his family in his fifties to live as a hermit and later mediated a crisis that averted civil war.
en.body: Nicholas of Flue lived an ordinary life in rural Switzerland as a farmer, respected local magistrate, and soldier before, at nearly fifty and with his wife's consent, he left his family of ten children to live as a hermit in a nearby ravine, surviving, by widely reported and much-debated tradition, on the Eucharist alone for the final decades of his life without other food. His reputation for wisdom and holiness spread, and in 1481, when the Swiss cantons were on the brink of collapsing into civil war over a bitter political dispute, delegates in desperation sought his counsel; his proposed compromise, delivered through a messenger since he rarely left his hermitage, was accepted by all sides and is credited with preserving Swiss unity. He is honored today as a father of the Swiss Confederation as much as a religious figure. He died in 1487 and was canonized in 1947.
